mn86:3.14: “Don’t take this road, ascetic. On this road there is a bandit named Aṅgulimāla. He is violent, bloody-handed, a hardened killer, merciless to living beings. He has laid waste to villages, towns, and countries.
mn86:3.15: He is constantly murdering humans, and he wears their fingers as a necklace.
mn86:3.16: People travel along this road only after banding closely together in groups of ten, twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty.
mn86:3.17: Still they meet their end by Aṅgulimāla’s hand.”

mn86:14.7: “Sir, this morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
mn86:14.8: Then, sir, as I was wandering indiscriminately for almsfood in Sāvatthī I saw a woman undergoing a distressing obstructed labor.
mn86:14.9: Seeing this, it occurred to me,
mn86:14.10: ‘Oh, beings undergo such travail! Oh, beings undergo such travail!’”
